The board did the job it was built for twice: c-0001.1's stated rationale was wrong and Claude Code checked the premise before doing the work rather than after, and the same-bar twin it found while recomputing H11 is a rule-3 violation that would have shipped as a flattering number. items.title: Measure the intraday alignment anchor before the 1-minute bar window closes
items.why: The daily anchor is proven at 98.8% vs 2.9%, but Phase 6 is an intraday timing study and it joins the same two clock domains at minute resolution, where a one-bar offset manufactures a clean spurious result instead of degrading a real one. This is the only item on the board with an external deadline: yfinance serves 1-minute bars for roughly 30 days and the dense intraday era starts 2026-08-19, so the measurement becomes impossible around 2026-09-18. Everything else can wait; this cannot.
items.acceptance: src/zoltar_ranks/analysis/alignment_anchor.py measures the intraday anchor at 1-minute resolution over the dense era and records a verdict in docs/FINDINGS.md with a Wilson interval, using the same PASS/reconcile discipline as the daily anchor. tests/test_alignment_anchor.py pins the intraday verdict alongside the daily one. If it fails, rule 9 applies — Phase 6 stops rather than the anchor being widened.

items.title: Move the twin-commit exclusion out of H11 and into shared available_at logic
items.why: You found that a forward-stamped evening retrain pairs with its own twin pushed 13 seconds later in the same commit, returning exactly 0.000% — 27 of 138 runs, satisfying rule 5 and the letter of rule 3 while biasing every statistic in the flattering direction. It is fixed inside the H11 power calculation. Left there, every future study re-derives it or silently inherits the bias, and the one that forgets will be the one that produces a headline number. This is the single most transferable thing found so far.
items.acceptance: The twin-commit exclusion lives in the shared available_at path (src/zoltar_ranks/analysis/execution.py or the ranks_pit view), not in h11_power.py; h11_power.py consumes it rather than implementing it; a contract test asserts a same-commit twin pair can never reach a backtest input path, and it FAILS against a fixture that admits one. Recomputing H11 reproduces the published MDE unchanged.
